title: Gregory of Valencia: God's motions and our responses
source_text: XXX. Rursus autem Gregorius de Valentia, clarioris doctrinae causa, motus qui ad actualem gratiam reducuntur, in duo genera distinguit. Unum, inquit, continetur iis motibus, quibus Deus mentes nostras excitat, vocat, & invitat, ut ad ipsum per fidem, spem, charitatem, poenitentiam, & hujusmodi actiones convertantur. Alterum continetur his motibus, seu actionibus, quibus Deo excitanti, vocanti, & invitanti respondemus, & aperimus mentis nostrae januam, quum ad eum convertimur. Tomo 2. Disput. 8. quaestione 3. puncto 2.
pass_a_gloss: XXX. But again Gregory of Valencia, for the sake of clearer doctrine, distinguishes the motions which are reduced to actual grace, into two kinds. One, he says, is contained in those motions, by which God excites, calls, and invites our minds, that they may be converted to him through faith, hope, charity, repentance, and actions of this sort. The other is contained in these motions, or actions, by which we respond to God exciting, calling, and inviting, and open the door of our mind, when we are converted to him. Tome 2 Disput. 8 question 3 point 2.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXX. Gregory of Valencia, to make the teaching clearer, divides the motions that belong to actual grace into two kinds.

'One kind,' he says, 'consists of the motions by which God rouses, calls and invites our minds to turn to him through faith, hope, charity, repentance and acts of that sort. The other consists of the motions or acts by which we answer God as he rouses, calls and invites us, and open the door of our mind when we turn to him' (tome 2, disputation 8, question 3, point 2).
